This article makes it sound like state officials actually take over and work at the physical locations in town. What actually happens is you have to pay your taxes and conduct other traditional town office business straight to the state through it's office in Augusta. Troopers pass by irregularly. Instead of a police state the townships are more or less left to themselves. Some even maintain their roads and other infrastructure through home-owners associations. The amount of government interference is actually reduced and local control in increased. For example, an association may charge $200 a year to every lot owner. The owner must also pay taxes to the state at a drastically lower mill rate that an organized town. Most of the money that the association collects goes to maintaining roads.
